newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile stocks end firm, focus on Enersis.
newsitem.headline: Chile stocks end firm, focus on Enersis.

text.p: Chilean blue chips closed higher in brisk trade with the market disbelieving power utility Enersis' denial that it is in talks to sell shares in generator Endesa to a Spanish electricity firm, said traders.
The bolsa is seen opening steady with trading in Enersis expected to continue dominate dealing, they said.
The selective IPSA index ended unofficially up 0.17 percent at 96.04 points. The general IGPA index gained 0.01 percent to 5,289.51 points.
Turnover doubled to 10.9 billion pesos from five billion pesos Monday with heavy buying from foreign investors.

Enersis and its associated companies were among the leading gainers on media reports that the firm is in negotiations to sell its 25 percent holding in Endesa for around $1 billion to the Spanish state utility, also known as Endesa, said dealers.
Enersis, which also has investments in distributors Chilectra and Rio Maipo, flatly denied the reports.
"Endesa shares have not been offered for sale to any company or national or foreign bank, so the information published today lacks all foundation," said corporate affairs manager Jaime Ale.
Despite this denial, investors believe that talks between the two companies are going on, said traders.
Enersis firmed 1.31 percent to 252 pesos. Associated investment companies Luz y Fuerza A and Almendros A rose 2.53 percent to 162 pesos and 2.52 percent to 163 pesos respectively.

Traders said the market's mood was dampened by speculation the government will set next year's inflation target at 5.5 percent, which would mean the Central Bank will probably not cut interest rates in the near future.
The government will release economic targets for 1997, including the inflation goal, in Congress Wednesday.
Losers included paper-maker CMPC, down 1.57 percent at 5,000 pesos, forestry firm Masisa, down 1.27 percent at 195 pesos and telecom Entel, which shed 1.09 percent to 3,630 pesos.
